To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the inclusion of selected phospholipids into liposomes can be used to modulate the immune response, (ii) liposome-encapsulated phospholipids can be used to target and activate the immune system, and (iii), this strategy can be used for the prevention or treatment of infectious diseases.
liposomes are efficient drug and antigen delivery systems that are currently used in the clinic for the treatment of several infections.
the use of liposomes as carriers of bioactive phospholipes could represent an innovative strategy in the prevention and/or treatment of infections.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of liposomes as vehicles for the delivery of bioactive molecules and as immunostimulatory agents.
the use of liposomes as a multifaceted approach for the treatment of infectious diseases.

the design and development of novel liposomes with multifunctional properties to improve drug or antigen delivery and to simultaneously activate specific antimicrobial pathways to prevent and/or treat infectious diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
liposomes can be used not only as a delivery tool for drugs or antigents but also as a multifunctional tool to modulate immune response.
liposomes can be considered as a multifaceted tool for the development of novel therapeutic and prophylactic strategies against infections.

the liposomes are a very promising and flexible system that can be used in a broad spectrum of therapeutic and prophylactic applications, from the treatment of chronic and recurrent infections to the development of novel vaccine formulations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
liposome-based formulations can be used to deliver drugs or antigens to target cells and simultaneously activate the immune response to fight infections.
liposomes are more than just drug or antigen delivery systems.

liposomes can be used as efficient drug or antigen carriers to induce an adaptive immune response against pathogens, while the lipid bilayer can be engineered to simultaneously induce an innate immune response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
liposomes represent a versatile platform to simultaneously deliver bioactive molecules and lipids with immunomodulatory functions.
the liposome platform can be exploited to develop novel immunomodulating formulations to improve the efficacy of vaccines and to treat chronic, recurrent, and drug-resistant infectious diseases.
the liposomes can be used not only to deliver the drug or the antigen to the target cells but also to modulate the immune response of the host to enhance its ability to fight against pathogens.
